claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for rollout is policy-compliant and evidentially supported despite a known material weakness in the logistics customs triage segment, based on aggregate readiness, rehearsal results, monitoring controls, and proposed model-card disclosure.
decision_criteria: A compliant certification requires admissible evidence that the material weakness is either excluded from rollout or covered by reviewed risk acceptance.
If the affected segment remains exposed, rollback switches, dashboards, small rollout percentage, and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties.
Supportive public guidance on model cards and risk management can reinforce the decision, but release-specific policy predicates must still be met.
The verdict turns on whether the required support link is evidenced in the record, not on whether the actor offers a plausible governance rationale.
evidence_requests: Final approved model card showing explicit disclosure of the logistics customs triage limitation and the affected tariff-code exception weakness.
Approved rollout gate or cohort definition proving the affected use case is excluded from initial exposure, if that is the intended mitigation.
Reviewed and signed risk-acceptance record that specifically addresses the exposed logistics customs triage segment and explains why exposure is acceptable.
Release decision artifact tying the certification decision to the actual disclosure and mitigation conditions, not just aggregate readiness metrics.
specific_concerns: The policy requires rollout controls to mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable.
The available summary says the affected logistics customs triage segment remains exposed in the initial rollout.
The available summary says the risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not address the exposed segment, so reviewed risk acceptance is not established.
The actor's position depends on explicit model-card disclosure of the limitation, but no admissible evidence is provided showing the actual model card contains that disclosure.
Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one incidents, rollback capability, and monitoring are supportive context but do not satisfy the missing policy predicate on their own.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant as locked on the present record.
That rollout monitoring and rollback controls are sufficient mitigation for the exposed weak segment without exclusion or reviewed risk acceptance.
That the required model-card disclosure has actually been made, rather than merely proposed as the condition under which certification would be defensible.
